claim: The BioInitiative Report — the source of the power-density 'effect threshold' charts that circulate through the EMF-safety movement — is a self-published document, first posted online in 2007 and updated in 2012, assembled by a self-selected group and edited by Cindy Sage and David Carpenter. It is not a peer-reviewed publication and is not a recognized exposure-standards body: the World Health Organization recognizes only the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP) and the IEEE for that role. Reviews by government and independent scientific bodies — including the EU's SCENIHR, the Australian and Dutch health authorities, and the IEEE Committee on Man and Radiation (COMAR) — criticized it as a selective rather than comprehensive review of the literature, inconsistent between chapters, and lacking balance. Its conclusions are a minority position advocating precautionary limits far below the ICNIRP/FCC thermal standards, not an established scientific consensus.
